title: Two Sum
statement_md:
Given an integer array `nums` and an integer `target`, return the indices of the two numbers that add up to `target`.

Every input has exactly one solution, and the same element may not be used twice. Return the indices in any order.

tests.explain_on_fail: Negative numbers have complements too: -3 pairs with 3.

editorial_md: Remember each value's index in a hash map. For every element, look up its complement `target - x` before storing it: one pass, O(n) time and O(n) space.

hints.body_md: Every number needs exactly one partner. What would make finding that partner instant?
A hash map from value to index answers "have I already seen `target - x`?" in O(1).

```
for i, x in nums:
    if target - x in seen: return [seen[target - x], i]
    seen[x] = i
```
